title: Caldera, Vidya add to recent flurry of biotech mergers
excerpt: The startups are part of a surge of young companies equipped with advanced drug prospects and quickly pivoting to the public markets.
content_html:
Gwendolyn Wu

Wed, July 29, 2026 at 8:07 AM EDT 2 min read

This story was originally published on BioPharma Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily BioPharma Dive newsletter.

Caldera Therapeutics and Vidya Therapeutics have struck a pair of deals with struggling biotechnology firms, according to company announcements made Wednesday.

Caldera, which launched just seven months ago with $112.5 million in venture funding, will merge with Synlogic. It's also brought in $278 million in a concurrent private financing to support a drug prospect licensed from China's Qyuns Therapeutics.

Called CLD-423, that drug aims at the proteins TL1A and IL-23p19, two well-known drug targets involved in inflammation. Caldera is testing it in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. Phase 1 testing is currently underway, with data expected by the end of 2026. The merger cash should fund the company through Phase 2 development.

Synlogic, Caldera's merger partner, went public via its own reverse merger in 2017. But its lead program struggled against the rare genetic disorder phenylketonuria and, in 2024, the company announced it would seek strategic alternatives and lay off about 90% of its staff.

Caldera is the latest participant in a recent run of merger deals involving biotechs built around China-licensed assets. Avere Therapeutics and Serapha Bio have both announced similar pacts over the last month. 

Others with advanced drug prospects are finding better access to the public markets, too. Vidya has a candidate called VT-7208 that it sees as having potential treating conditions such as food allergies, chronic spontaneous urticaria and relapsing multiple sclerosis. That drug's nearing Phase 2 testing, and an acquisition by Processa Pharmaceuticals announced Wednesday will support the effort.

Like Caldera, Vidya also announced a sizable financing alongside its acquisition — a $200 million private funding from more than 10 firms. 

VT-7208 is a newer type of so-called Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor. These drugs are best known for their impact on blood cancers, but drugmakers in recent years have developed prospects that can slip past the blood-brain barrier and potentially treat neurological conditions or immune diseases.

Vidya faces stiff competition. Sanofi's tolebrutinib is approved in Europe for a form of MS. Roche is nearing a potential clearance a different BTK blocker in relapsing disease.

The combined company will continue developing two drugs Processa was studying in breast cancer and gastrointestinal conditions as well, though it will continue "evaluating strategic opportunities designed to maximize their clinical and long-term value," according to the announcement.

Both deals announced Wednesday are expected to help fund company operations into 2029.

根据周三发布的公司公告，Caldera Therapeutics 和 Vidya Therapeutics 已与陷入困境的生物技术公司达成了两项交易。

Caldera 刚刚在 7 个月前推出，获得了 1.125 亿美元的风险投资，该公司将与 Synlogic 合并。 它还通过同时进行的私人融资筹集了 2.78 亿美元，以支持中国 Qyuns Therapeutics 许可的药物前景。

该药物名为 CLD-423，针对蛋白质 TL1A 和 IL-23p19，这是两个与炎症有关的众所周知的药物靶点。 Caldera 正在测试其治疗溃疡性结肠炎和克罗恩病的效果。 第一阶段测试目前正在进行中，预计将于 2026 年底提供数据。 合并现金将为公司完成第二阶段的开发提供资金。

Caldera 的合并伙伴 Synlogic 于 2017 年通过反向并购上市。 但其主导项目却与罕见的遗传性疾病苯丙酮尿症作斗争，2024 年，该公司宣布将寻求战略替代方案，并解雇约 90% 的员工。

Caldera 是最近一系列并购交易的最新参与者，这些并购交易涉及围绕中国许可资产建立的生物技术公司。 Avere Therapeutics 和 Serapha Bio 上个月都宣布了类似的协议。

其他具有先进药物前景的公司也正在寻找更好的进入公开市场的机会。 Vidya 有一种名为 VT-7208 的候选药物，它认为该药物具有潜在的治疗食物过敏、慢性自发性荨麻疹和复发性多发性硬化症等病症的潜力。 该药物即将进行第二阶段测试，周三 Processa Pharmaceuticals 宣布的收购将支持这一努力。

与 Caldera 一样，Vidya 在收购的同时也宣布了一笔巨额融资——来自 10 多家公司的 2 亿美元私人融资。

VT-7208 是一种新型的所谓布鲁顿酪氨酸激酶抑制剂。 这些药物因其对血癌的影响而闻名，但近年来制药商已经开发出可以突破血脑屏障并有可能治疗神经系统疾病或免疫疾病的前景。

维迪亚面临着激烈的竞争。 赛诺菲的托布替尼在欧洲被批准用于治疗一种多发性硬化症。 罗氏（Roche）正在接近清除另一种 BTK 阻滞剂治疗复发性疾病的可能性。

公告称，合并后的公司将继续开发 Processa 正在研究的两种用于乳腺癌和胃肠道疾病的药物，但该公司将继续“评估旨在最大化其临床和长期价值的战略机会”。

周三宣布的两项交易预计将为公司 2029 年的运营提供资金。
